Fit spatial models to examine spatial heterogeneity in the ATE in AVENIR

2026-03-05

source(here::here("0-config.R"))

df_all <- readRDS(here("data","mortality_analysis_dataset.rds")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(adaptive_rand == "Randomization 1")

# Project coordinates to UTM so distances are in meters, not degrees

df_proj <- df_all %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 32631) %>% # UTM zone 31N, for Niger
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2])
plot_matern_corr_proj <- function(spamm_model_fit, 
                                  filenameval="avenir-materncorr") {
  
  # create a distance matrix between all points
  coords <- as.matrix(spamm_model_fit$data[, c("lon","lat")])
  d_vec_m <- as.numeric(dist(coords))
  
  # get estimated parameters from the Matern function
  est_nu <- spamm_model_fit$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars$`1`$nu
  est_rho <- spamm_model_fit$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars$`1`$rho
  
  rho_sci <- format(est_rho, scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)
  range_km <- 1/(1000*est_rho)
  
  # estimate the correlation between each location
  matern_vec <- spaMM::MaternCorr(d = d_vec_m, nu = est_nu, rho = est_rho)
  
  # store in a data frame for plotting
  d_matern_cor <- tibble(
    distm = d_vec_m,
    distkm = distm/1000,
    materncor = matern_vec) %>%
    mutate(bin_km = cut(distkm, breaks = seq(0, max(distkm), by = 0.025), include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(bin_km) %>%
    summarise(
      distkm    = mean(distkm),
      materncor = mean(materncor),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(distkm)
  
  label_text <- sprintf("nu = %0.3f\rho = %0.3f\nrange = %0.2f km", est_nu, est_rho, range_km)
  
  #--------------------------------------
  # plot the correlation function
  #--------------------------------------
  plot_materncor <- ggplot(data = d_matern_cor %>% filter(distkm<=50)) +
    # geom_point(aes(x=distms,y=distkm)) +
    geom_point(aes(x=distkm, y = materncor),color="black",alpha=1,size=0.1) + 
    # geom_vline(xintercept= 3 ,color="gray60", lwd=0.1) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,by=0.2)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0,seq(10,50,by=10))) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim=c(0,50),ylim=c(0,1)) +
    labs(x="distance (km)",y = "Matern correlation") +
    annotate("text",
             x = 15, y = 0.90,
             label = as.expression(bquote(nu == .(format(est_nu, digits = 3)))),
             hjust = 0, size = 6) +
    
    annotate("text",
             x = 15, y = 0.80,
             label = as.expression(bquote(rho == .(rho_sci) ~ m^{-1})),
             hjust = 0, size = 6) +
    
    annotate("text",
             x = 15, y = 0.65,
             label = as.expression(bquote(range == .(format(range_km, digits = 4)) ~ km)),
             hjust = 0, size = 6) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_text(size=16),
      axis.title = element_text(size=18)
    )
  
  ggsave(filename=paste0(figure_path,filenameval,".png"),
         plot=plot_materncor,
         device="png",
         width=3.3,
         height=3.5)
  
  return(plot_materncor)
  
}

Simple Kriging model

Fit model

# fit spatial models for mortality rate with new binary tx vars,
# isTreated_child: 0=placebo+infant, 1=child
# isTreated_alltx: 0=placebo, 1=infant+child

avail_thr <- parallel::detectCores(logical=FALSE) - 1L 

tic("Simple Krig: fit spaMM model for child mortality")
fitmort_child_simp_krig <- spaMM::fitme(
  n_deaths_1to59 ~
    1 +
    Matern(1 | lat + lon) +
    isTreated_child +
    # (1|site_code) +
    offset(log(pt_year_1to59)),
  data = df_proj,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  control.HLfit = list(NbThreads = avail_thr)
)
## (One-time message:) Choosing matrix methods took 1.27 s.
##   If you perform many similarly costly fits, setting the method
##   by control.HLfit=list(algebra=<"spprec"|"spcorr"|"decorr">) may be useful,
##   see help("algebra"). "decorr" has been selected here.
toc()
## Simple Krig: fit spaMM model for child mortality: 1056.744 sec elapsed
saveRDS(fitmort_child_simp_krig, here("data","fitmort_child_simp_krig.rds"))

Summary

summary(fitmort_child_simp_krig)
## formula: n_deaths_1to59 ~ 1 + Matern(1 | lat + lon) + isTreated_child + 
##     offset(log(pt_year_1to59))
## Estimation of corrPars and lambda by ML (p_v approximation of logL).
## Estimation of fixed effects by ML (p_v approximation of logL).
## Estimation of lambda by 'outer' ML, maximizing logL.
## family: poisson( link = log ) 
##  ------------ Fixed effects (beta) ------------
##                          Estimate Cond. SE t-value
## (Intercept)                -4.328  0.12400 -34.905
## isTreated_childTreatment   -0.173  0.04322  -4.003
##  --------------- Random effects ---------------
## Family: gaussian( link = identity ) 
##                    --- Correlation parameters:
##         1.nu        1.rho 
## 1.410592e-01 1.696902e-05 
##            --- Variance parameters ('lambda'):
## lambda = var(u) for u ~ Gaussian; 
##    lat + lon  :  0.2121  
## # of obs: 1390; # of groups: lat + lon, 1390 
##  ------------- Likelihood values  -------------
##                         logLik
## logL       (p_v(h)): -2493.581

Generalized kriging model

Fit model

tic("Generalized Krig: fit spaMM model for child mortality with linear lat/lon terms")
fitmort_child_gen_krig <- spaMM::fitme(
  n_deaths_1to59 ~
    1 +
    lat + lon +
    Matern(1 | lat + lon) +
    isTreated_child +
    # (1|site_code) +
    offset(log(pt_year_1to59)),
  data = df_proj,
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  control.HLfit = list(NbThreads = avail_thr)
)
toc()
## Generalized Krig: fit spaMM model for child mortality with linear lat/lon terms: 752.615 sec elapsed
saveRDS(fitmort_child_gen_krig, here("data","fitmort_child_gen_krig.rds"))

Compare to simple model

AIC(fitmort_child_simp_krig)
AIC(fitmort_child_gen_krig)

LRT(fitmort_child_gen_krig, fitmort_child_simp_krig)
##      chi2_LR df     p_value
## p_v 13.14651  2 0.001397244

LRT and AIC indicate that adding linear terms for latitude and longitude significantly improves model fit, i.e., the generalized krige model is preferred over the simple krige.

Generalized krig with interaction

Fit model

tic("fit spaMM model for child mortality with interaction")
fitmort_child_gen_krig_int <- spaMM::fitme(n_deaths_1to59 ~ 
                                   1 + lat + lon + 
                                   Matern(1|lat + lon) +
                                   isTreated_child +
                                   isTreated_child*lat + isTreated_child*lon +
                                   # (1|site_code) +
                                   offset(log(pt_year_1to59)),
                                 data = df_proj,
                                 family = poisson(link = "log"),
                                 control.HLfit=list(NbThreads = avail_thr))
toc()
## fit spaMM model for child mortality with interaction: 928.029 sec elapsed
saveRDS(fitmort_child_gen_krig_int, here("data","fitmort_child_gen_krig_int.rds"))

Compare to generalized krig model

AIC(fitmort_child_gen_krig)
AIC(fitmort_child_gen_krig_int)

LRT(fitmort_child_gen_krig_int, fitmort_child_gen_krig)
##      chi2_LR df    p_value
## p_v 8.117922  2 0.01726695

LRT and AIC indicate that the model with the interaction between treatment label and latitude and longitude fits better than the one without interaction.
